explanation: Saving means keeping money for later. Spending means using money to buy something now. It's good to do a little of both!
A need is something we can't live without, like food or shoes. A want is something we would like to have, like a new toy.
Money comes in small coins and bigger notes. Together they help us pay for things we need and want.
Sometimes we have to wait and save a little every day until we have enough money to buy something special.
A piggy bank is a little box where we keep our coins. Every time we save a coin, we get closer to our goal.
When we pay with more money than something costs, we get change back: the extra money that is returned to us.
People work to earn money. Helping at home can also teach us the value of effort.
We can use a little of our money to help others, like giving a gift to a friend.
A budget is a plan that shows how much money we have and how we will spend or save it. It helps us avoid spending more than we have.
A bank is a safe place where people keep their money. It can also help us save and make our money grow.
Before buying, it's smart to check the price of the same thing at different stores. That way we pick the cheaper option.
A discount happens when a store lowers the price of something for a while. But it's worth checking if it's really a true saving.
A savings goal is deciding what we want to save money for, like a toy or a trip. Having a goal helps us want to save more.
Nowadays, money can also be digital, kept on a card or phone instead of coins and notes. It's still real money!
Sometimes we borrow money from someone and promise to pay it back later. It's important to always keep that promise.
Not everything costs the same. Knowing the value of money helps us tell if something is expensive or cheap for what it offers.
